subject: Re: Dedicated pool — overage handling, escrow credits & metering
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@acme.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Aug 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool: handling above-commit bursts & credits

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking this — quick context: Acme.ai is sizing a Dedicated GPU pool for inference over the next 18 months. We expect steady baseline traffic with occasional multi-hour bursts during model retraining validations and marketing-led demos.

Before we proceed with a commit, procurement needs clarity on:
- How over-commit usage is metered (per-minute GPU usage, per-GPU-hour, or token-level?)
- Whether Redwood supports a refundable / pre-funded credit (escrow) to cover burst usage instead of pay-as-you-go overage invoices
- Throttling policy: at what point do you throttle vs queue vs fallback to hosted models?
- Overage rate bands and any discounts if we bump committed capacity mid-term

I've attached a small CSV with our expected hourly percentiles for the next quarter (acme-expected-traffic.csv).

We have a tight procurement window (finalizing terms week of 8/20). Can you outline options and an example invoice for a 1-week high spike?

Best,
Samantha Lee
Procurement Manager, Acme.ai
procure@acme.ai

--
Attachment: acme-expected-traffic.csv (CSV, 42KB)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@acme.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Aug 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool: handling above-commit bursts & credits

Samantha — thanks for the CSV and the clear ask. Looping in Laura (commercial) and Monica (operations) to cover pricing + runtime behavior. High-level options we can offer:

1) Soft-burst buffer + hourly metering
- Metering: we bill overage as GPU-seconds aggregated hourly (so you can map to your tooling).
- Throttling: soft-burst keeps requests unthrottled up to a short buffer (1–2 minutes) then applies prioritized scheduling; we won't drop requests unless you explicitly enable strict throttle policies.
- Overage rate: standard overage = 1.6x committed unit price; for committed increases we can tier downward.

2) Pre-funded surge escrow (recommended for procurement)
- You pre-fund a surge account (USD credit) that draws down on overages. Monthly true-up + refundable if unused at term end (subject to MSA addendum).
- Benefit: predictable cashflow, single invoice cadence, and automatic failover to allow spikes without throttling during critical windows.

3) Hybrid: guaranteed baseline throughput with pay-as-you-go burst lanes at a capped hourly rate

Attached is a short one-pager summarizing these options (redwood-dedicated-overage-options.pdf). Monica — can you confirm the exact throttling heuristics (priority bump, KV cache preservation, and fallback to hosted) and whether we can surface GPU-second granularity in their billing export?

Samantha — happy to run a sample invoice once we pick an option. If you want, we can propose a 3-month pilot with an escrow and capped overage rate to meet your procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.inference.com

--
Attachment: redwood-dedicated-overage-options.pdf (PDF, 96KB)
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.inference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@acme.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool: handling above-commit bursts & credits

Hi Samantha — thanks for the signal. Commercial proposal below (high level) — we can convert to an SOW/MSA addendum once you confirm the approach.

Recommended commercial structure:
- Baseline commit: 200 GPU-hours/day (monthly billing cadence). 12-month term recommended to secure discount.
- Discount ladder: 0–199 baseline -> list price; 200–599 -> 8% discount; 600+ -> 15% discount on committed units.
- Overage treatment: two tracks:
  a) Escrow track: pre-funded surge credit that draws at 1.25x committed rate; unused funds refundable at contract renewal/termination on a pro-rata basis.
  b) Pay-as-you-go track: invoiced monthly at 1.6x committed rate, with true-up.
- Throttle semantics: after sustained 10-minute window above 3x baseline we engage prioritized queuing; in extreme spikes (>5x baseline sustained >30m) we will route to compatible lower-cost variants (if configured) and notify with immediate mitigation steps.

Operational asks for pilot:
- 30-day pilot with a $50k surge escrow; Redwood will provide a sample invoice and daily burn-rate dashboard.
- Billing export delivered as CSV with per-hour GPU-second rows and aggregated daily totals.

Attached: proposed-pricing-sheet.xlsx (contains sample invoice calculations and a 30-day pilot pro forma). Also linking a DocuSign powerform for a standard MSA addendum: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?powerFormId=abcd-1234

If that looks good, Rishi/Monica — please prepare the pilot statement and the pilot monitoring dashboard access. Samantha — can you confirm procurement's preferred escrow mechanics (pre-pay card vs wire) and signatory details so we can generate the DocuSign?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Commercial Sales | Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.inference.com

--
Attachment: proposed-pricing-sheet.xlsx (XLSX, 28KB)
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@acme.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Acme.ai Procurement <procure@acme.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool: handling above-commit bursts & credits

Laura / Rishi — appreciate the clear options. Procurement is comfortable with the escrow track for the pilot. A few follow-ups before we sign:

1) Metering granularly: we want the per-hour GPU-second export (that matches your billing CSV). Please include one sample invoice calculation in the Doc you will send so our finance team can map to our AP process.

2) Throttling SLA: in the event of a large marketing-driven spike (multi-hour >4x baseline) we need a written fallback that prevents silent silent drop of critical inference requests during demos. Is the "route to lower-cost variant" automatic or requires config? We prefer automatic fallback with explicit opt-out via config.

3) Escrow mechanics: we prefer wire for the pre-fund. Can you include wiring instructions in the DocuSign flow and a contact for refunds at termination?

If you can send the pilot DocuSign this afternoon with sample invoice and wiring instructions, procurement can complete review by 8/20.

Thanks —
Samantha Lee
Procurement Manager, Acme.ai
procure@acme.ai
